title: A distinctive smell from breath, skin, or body fluids near death

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
The record must not be used to diagnose, time, or manage a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, and emergency decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: In the last days, witnesses may notice a strong, unfamiliar, sweet, chemical, acetone-like, urine-like, or illness-specific smell in the room, on breath, skin, bedding, or body fluids.

content_layers.observation_text: One public hospice source describes distinctive smells from breath, skin, and body fluids near death, including an acetone-like comparison and possible stronger smells in some gastrointestinal cancers.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Hospice UK currently supports this as a single-source public pilot; it should remain quarantined until clinical review and witness testimony broaden it.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: The seed warned that smell is easy to miss. This record deliberately opens a smell lane while keeping it single-source and non-sensational.

what_this_is_not: not a diagnosis of a particular disease
not a claim that every death has a distinctive smell
not a reason for shame or disgust
uncertainties: Only one public source is currently entered.
Smell is highly subjective, culturally mediated, and difficult to write without voyeurism.
The record needs hospice, nursing, funeral, and caregiver testimony.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should acknowledge that smell can be part of dying without making the body sound shameful or grotesque.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect practical and verbal responses to smell: ventilation, bedding, hygiene, disease explanation, and dignity language, all under care-team review.
language_notes: Smell words must be specific but not lurid.
Search aliases should include frightening phrases while the rendered surface stays calm.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the v2 witnessed-moment schema. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical safety review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent or worried readers to qualified local support.
